title: 27 days of vibe coding my game with GPT-6.1 Sol. Here's my progress!
author: ExtraBroBro
selftext:
I've been working on my own game for 27 days using AI. I started with GPT-6 Astra but later switched to GPT-6.1 Sol because it uses around 5–10 times less of my usage limit while giving me similar results for most tasks. One of the biggest challenges was optimization. At first, 400 monsters could drop the game to 5 FPS, but after almost two weeks of testing and improving the code, it can now handle up to 1,000 monsters. The visuals and animations also need a lot of manual work. It's still an early prototype, but here's a short look at my progress! I'd love to hear your feedback, especially from anyone else using AI for game development.  
Full video: [https://youtu.be/mJx\_IWZdCPo](https://youtu.be/mJx_IWZdCPo)

comments.author: ConsultioGames
comments.body: The combat looks frustrating as hell, the giant nice looking snake water thing missed 90% of its attacks too?

replies.author: ExtraBroBro
replies.body: Yeah, I noticed that too while playing I've tested combat before, but not with such large groups of enemies and multiple skills at once. Cooldowns aren't implemented yet, and there's still a lot of balancing to do, especially with attack accuracy. I just wanted to share the current progress before polishing it further. Could make a nice before-and-after video later! Glad you liked how the Water Serpent looks though! :D

comments.author: StoneBladeMaster
comments.body: What sort of prompt did you do for the animations and vfx? I find that codex has had trouble doing good 2d pixel animations which I’m sure is a user problem, but I can’t really figure out what’s going on.  Your attack visuals look awesome and would love to learn how to get that vibe

replies.author: ExtraBroBro
replies.body: Thanks! Really glad you like the effects! I actually make the sprite animations by hand. For VFX, I use a custom tool called SkillFactory that Codex built for me. The interesting part is that I designed it specifically for AI to use, rather than making it convenient for humans. So now I can basically vibe code my VFX too! I just describe what I want, and Codex can create and adjust the effects directly in the tool.

replies.author: sgeep
replies.body:
Sounds like a top priority should be reworking your Codex app to keep the styling consistent with the rest of the project

Right now it looks a bit all over the place, which also gives it that pretty generic "AI" look

replies.author: ExtraBroBro
replies.body: Yeah, that's exactly what I'm thinking about right now! I definitely need to make the VFX style more consistent with the rest of the game. I'm still figuring out the best way to achieve that without losing what I like about the effects. Thanks for the feedback!

comments.author: Saytron3030
comments.body: Bros non pixelated water snake from another universe only does 7 damage smh

comments.author: GooRedSpeakers
comments.body: This looks really good. I like the idea of a JRPG style CRPG with mouse aiming and horde combat. This is a cool project. If I may make a suggestion, maybe adding Leage of Legends/DotA style skill aiming tooltips would help make those realtime skill shots easier to land.

replies.author: ExtraBroBro
replies.body: Thank you so much! Really glad you like the project! Right now I only have smart casting, so skills activate immediately based on the cursor position. But I'll definitely think about adding aiming indicators like you suggested. I think that could make combat feel much better. Thanks for the idea!

comments.author: Comet7777
comments.body: You’re mixing a ton of different art styles. Like when that meteor hit, that wasn’t pixelated really. So get some uniformity here and it’ll help, otherwise it’s distracting and points at obvious AI usage

replies.author: ExtraBroBro
replies.body: I actually agree with you! It's still pretty hard for me to tell which effects fit the game's art style and which ones stand out too much. I've already noticed this problem with some of my skills, but I'm still learning to recognize these differences. It's definitely something I need to work on. Thanks for the feedback!

comments.author: JuanDMGG
comments.body: can you make a tutorial about how to do a game like that, would love to see the whole video

replies.author: ExtraBroBro
replies.body: Yeah, I'll definitely make a tutorial in the future! It's actually already on my to-do list :D

comments.author: Varrianda
comments.body: Are the path and cliff tiles AI generated or human made assets? If they're AI I'm genuinely impressed

replies.author: ExtraBroBro
replies.body: Yes, they are AI-generated! But it took a lot of trial and error, many different prompts, and testing several AI models to get them looking the way I wanted. Definitely wasn't a one-prompt result! Glad you like how they turned out!

replies.author: ExtraBroBro
